title: Factors Associated With Residual Disease In The Central Cone
brief_summary: Cervical conization using the loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP) is the standard treatment for patients with high-grade cervical intraepithelial neoplasia. Several studies have shown that excising a central cone reduces the rate of positive endocervical margins. The purpose of this study is to identify clinicopathological factors associated with residual disease in the central cone and to develop a predictive model to better determine which patients may require this additional procedure.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* patients who underwent a loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP)

Exclusion Criteria:

* a diagnosis of micro-invasion or nonsquamous histology
* less than six months of follow-up
* incomplete information in their clinical charts.
study_population: patients who underwent a cervical cone procedure at the Dysplasia Clinic of the Instituto Nacional de Cancerologia in Mexico City
